requirements.statement: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g) || []; const bad = []; const tax = ['Floor – all brands']; for (const x of m) { const c = x.replace(/"category"\s*:\s*"/,'').replace(/"$/,''); if (!/^(Violence – minor|Violence – graphic|Dangerous acts|Language – mild|Language – strong|Firearms – depiction|Firearms – use|Disaster – news|Disaster – graphic|Alcohol – reference|Alcohol – consumption|Floor – all brands)$/.test(c)) bad.push({start:0,end:0,why:'category not exact in taxonomy: '+c}); } return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? bad.length+' unknown categories' : 'all categories exact', spans: bad }; }
means: Each category string in the label must match a taxonomy name exactly. The full 39-name list is not given in the outline, so this checks only the names shown; a partial list is used.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a timecode span, start–end in mm:ss, inside the clip's duration.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})–(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; const dur = (text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/)||[]); const D = dur.length? (+dur[1])*60+(+dur[2]) : null; while((m=re.exec(text))){ const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if(D!==null && e>D) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span past duration'}); } return {ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? bad.length+' spans past duration':'spans inside duration', spans: bad}; }
means: Each span must be in mm:ss–mm:ss form and end within the clip duration. Format is checked; the start-end pattern is matched.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a risk level: Low, Medium or High.

source: (text, request, material) => {
const bad = [];
const re = /"category"\s*:\s*"[^"]+"\s*,\s*"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g;
let m;
while ((m = re.exec(text))) {
const ok = /^(Low|Medium|High)$/.test(m[1]);
if (!ok && !/^(Floor)$/.test(m[1])) {
bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'risk not Low, Medium or High'});
return {ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' bad risk levels' : 'risk levels valid', spans: bad};
means: Each category entry's risk must be exactly Low, Medium or High.

requirements.statement: "High" risk requires an explicit depiction in the clip: a described act, injury, blood, a weapon fired, an explicit sexual act. A reference, a mention or a discussion is Medium at most.
A clip labelled "Firearms – depiction" or "Firearms – use" is never also labelled "Floor – all brands".

source: (text, request, material) => { const f=/Firearms – (depiction|use)/.test(text); const b=/Floor – all brands/.test(text); const ok = !(f&&b); return {ok, detail: ok?'no conflict':'Firearms label with Floor label', spans: ok?[]:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'Firearms and Floor both present'}]}; }
means: The label must not contain both a Firearms category and Floor – all brands.

requirements.statement: A clip with no flagged category is labelled "Floor – all brands" with risk Floor and no timecode.

source: (text, request, material) => { const hasCats = /"category"/.test(text); const floorOnly = /"Floor – all brands"/.test(text); if (hasCats) return {ok:true, detail:'flagged categories present; rule not triggered', spans:[]}; const ok = floorOnly && /"risk"\s*:\s*"Floor"/.test(text) && !/"span"/.test(text); return {ok, detail: ok?'clean clip labelled Floor with no span':'clean clip not labelled Floor, or has a span', spans: ok?[]:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'Floor rule broken'}]}; }
means: With no categories, the label must be Floor – all brands, risk Floor, and no span.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return { ok: true, detail: 'not JSON; skipped', spans: [] }; } const bad = []; for (const c of (obj.categories || [])) { if (!c.evidence || String(c.evidence).trim() === '') bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'flagged category with no evidence: ' + c.category }); } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' category(ies) without evidence' : 'all flagged categories carry evidence', spans: bad }; }
means: Each flagged category must have a non-empty evidence field. Whether the words are a true copy of the transcript is checked by step 17.

requirements.statement: "Violence – graphic" requires described injury or blood; a scuffle, a push or a threat is "Violence – minor".
"Language – strong" requires a word of the strong list in the transcript; "Language – mild" otherwise.
A label carries no category the transcript does not support with evidence.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return { ok: true, detail: 'not JSON; skipped', spans: [] }; } const bad = []; for (const c of (obj.categories || [])) { if (!c.evidence || String(c.evidence).trim() === '') bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'category with no evidence: ' + c.category }); } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' unsupported category(ies)' : 'every category has evidence', spans: bad }; }
means: Every category must carry evidence text. Whether the evidence actually supports the category is judgement.

requirements.statement: Risk is the highest of the flagged categories' risk levels, carried once at the top of the label as overall.

source: (text, request, material) => { const order={Low:1,Medium:2,High:3}; const risks=[...text.matchAll(/"risk"\s*:\s*"(Low|Medium|High)"/g)].map(m=>m[1]); const om=text.match(/"overall"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/); if(!om) return {ok:false,detail:'no overall',spans:[]}; if(!risks.length) return {ok:true,detail:'no flagged risks',spans:[]}; const top=risks.reduce((a,b)=>order[b]>order[a]?b:a); const ok=om[1]===top; return {ok, detail: ok?'overall equals highest risk':'overall is '+om[1]+', highest is '+top, spans: ok?[]:[{start:om.index,end:om.index+om[0].length,why:'overall mismatch'}]}; }
means: The overall value must equal the highest risk among the category entries.

requirements.statement: A span's end is after its start, and no span runs past the duration.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad=[]; const re=/"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})–(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if(e<=s) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'end not after start'}); } return {ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? bad.length+' spans end before start':'span order valid', spans: bad}; }
means: Each span's end is later than its start. The duration bound is checked under step 2.

requirements.statement: Where the same act is both "Violence" and "Dangerous acts", both are flagged, each with its own evidence.
A news report of a disaster is "Disaster – news", Medium at most; graphic footage described is "Disaster – graphic".
A reference to alcohol in passing is "Alcohol – reference", Low; drinking described is "Alcohol – consumption", Medium.
Numbers in a span are seconds and minutes only: no frame counts.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad=[]; const re=/"span"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ if(/\bf(rame)?s?\b|\bframe\b/i.test(m[1])) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'frame count in span'}); } return {ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? 'frame count found':'spans use seconds and minutes only', spans: bad}; }
means: A span must contain no frame word or frame count.

requirements.statement: Evidence is copied from the transcript, never paraphrased.

source: (text, request, material) => {
const norm = s => String(s).toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
const bad = [];
const tr = norm(material.map(m => m.text).join(' '));
let m;
while ((m = re.exec(text))) {
const ev = norm(m[1]);
if (ev && !tr.includes(ev) && !/nothing in the transcript is flagged/.test(ev)) {
bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'evidence not found verbatim in transcript'});
return {ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' evidence quotes not verbatim' : 'evidence matches transcript', spans: bad};
means: Each evidence string must appear verbatim in the material, ignoring case and spacing.

requirements.statement: A category flagged twice is listed once, with the earliest span.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad=[]; const seen=new Set(); const re=/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ if(seen.has(m[1])) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'category listed twice'}); seen.add(m[1]); } return {ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? bad.length+' repeated categories':'each category listed once', spans: bad}; }
means: No category name appears more than once in the categories list. Which span is earliest is not checked.

requirements.statement: The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.

source: (text, request, material) => { let o; try { o=JSON.parse(text); } catch(e) { return {ok:false,detail:'not valid JSON',spans:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'not JSON'}]}; } const keys=Object.keys(o).sort().join(','); const ok=keys==='categories,clip,duration,overall'; return {ok, detail: ok?'keys exact':'keys are '+keys, spans: ok?[]:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'key set differs'}]}; }
means: The label parses as JSON and has exactly the four keys clip, duration, overall, categories.

requirements.statement: Where a clip's transcript is empty, the label is "Floor – all brands" and says so in evidence.

source: (text, request, material) => { const tr=material.map(m=>m.text).join(' ').trim(); if(tr) return {ok:true,detail:'transcript not empty; rule not triggered',spans:[]}; const ok=/"Floor – all brands"/.test(text) && /"evidence"\s*:\s*"[^"]*(empty|no transcript|no speech)[^"]*"/i.test(text); return {ok, detail: ok?'empty transcript labelled Floor with evidence note':'empty transcript not handled', spans: ok?[]:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'empty transcript rule broken'}]}; }
means: If the transcript is empty, the label is Floor – all brands and the evidence says the transcript is empty.

requirements.statement: My pieces run 224 to 452 characters; a new piece stays between 1 and 680.
My pieces run 23 to 53 words; a new piece stays between 1 and 83.
My pieces run 1 sentence; a new piece has at most 2.
The longest sentence in my pieces runs 23 to 53 words; in a new piece it stays at most 83 words.
At most 24 line breaks: my pieces carry 12 to 18.
No blank lines: none of my pieces has one.
No hashtags: none of my pieces has one.
No mentions (@): none of my pieces has one.
No links: none of my pieces has one.
No emoji: none of my pieces has one.
Open on a claim, as my pieces do.
Close on a statement, as my pieces do.
The first word is a symbol or emoji, as in every piece of mine.
Quoted phrases: about 53 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Colons: about 28.2 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Figures written in digits: about 20.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Nominalisations (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ence): about 8.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Runs of five or more one-syllable words: about 2.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
I keep paragraphs to 2 sentences at most.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
